original_value: Web developers use base64 formats to include images, fonts, sounds, and other resources directly inside HTML, JavaScript, JSON, and XML files. We estimate that billions of base64 messages are decoded every day. We are motivated to improve the efficiency of base64 encoding and decoding. Compared to state-of-the-art implementations, we multiply the speeds of both the encoding (≈ 10 ×0) and the decoding (≈ 7 ×). We achieve these good results by using the single-instruction-multiple-data instructions available on recent Intel processors (AVX2). Our accelerated software abides by the specification and reports errors when encountering characters outside of the base64 set. It is available online as free software under a liberal license.

result.paraphrase: Base64 is used by web developers to embed images, fonts, sounds, and other resources directly in HTML, JavaScript, JSON, and XML files. We estimate that billions of base64 messages are decoded each day. To improve the efficiency of base64 encoding and decoding, we multiply the speed of encoding by about 10× and decoding by about 7× compared with state-of-the-art implementations. These results come from using the single-instruction multiple-data instructions available on recent Intel processors (AVX2). Our accelerated software follows the specification and reports errors when it encounters characters outside the base64 set. It is available online as free software under a liberal license.
